Description:
A torus cut by one of its VILLARCEAU PLANES - the only plane/torus contact that produces crossing
intersection curves.
The torus has major radius 20 and minor radius 10 about the z axis. A plane through its centre inclined
by alpha with sin alpha = r/R = 0.5, that is 30 degrees, is BITANGENT to it: it touches the torus at two
points and cuts it in two circles of radius R = 20, the Villarceau circles, which cross exactly at those
two tangential contact points
  (15, 0, -8.6602540378) and (-15, 0, 8.6602540378)
That is an inner tangential contact of a plane and a torus with a NODE of the intersection curve at both
contacts - the plane and the torus have the same tangent plane there and the two circles cross.

A torus can only do this where its Gaussian curvature is negative, and both contacts indeed sit on the
inner half of the tube: no plane can touch a convex piece of a surface and still cross it.

The plane is not rotated about the z axis, so both contacts land at y = 0 - in the xz plane, which is
exactly where a torus about the z axis through the origin is split into its half faces. Contact point,
node and seam coincide. TorusVillarceauPlaneOblique is the same case rotated by 37 degrees, where they
do not.

The cutting body is a slab: a 70 x 70 rectangle in the Villarceau plane, extruded 30 mm along the
inward normal. The torus fits into it completely - every torus point is at most 30 mm from the centre
and at most 20 mm below the plane - so the slab acts as an exact half space for this torus.
Expected:
V(torus) = 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 2*pi^2*20*100 = 4000*pi^2 = 39478.4176043574,
area 4*pi^2*R*r = 4*pi^2*200 = 7895.6835208715, extent -30,-30,-10 .. 30,30,10.
V(slab) = 70*70*30 = 147000.

The Villarceau plane passes through the centre of the torus, and the point reflection p -> -p maps the
torus onto itself while exchanging the two sides of the plane. The two parts are therefore CONGRUENT and
each is exactly half the torus:
  villarceauInter (the part inside the slab)   2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787
  villarceauRest  (the part outside)           2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787
Not a captured number but an exact one, and the two must agree with each other to the last digit.
  villarceauUnion  147000 + 19739.2088021787 = 166739.2088021787

Each half is a single solid that hangs together through the two contact points only, in the same way as
the two halves in EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam: at the two contacts the cut degenerates to a point. Both
halves are bounded by a piece of the torus and by the plane region between the two Villarceau circles,
which is a pair of crescents meeting at the two nodes - the ordinary annulus of a horizontal section,
degenerated. A half must not come out as a manifold body with a smooth boundary there, and must not be
reported as two separate solids of a quarter torus each.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. FIXED on 2026-08-28 by the second repair of the same day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). Two things changed at once and both were needed:
the geometry became RIGHT where it was wrong, and the face partition became REPRODUCIBLE - the case is
stable over 4 runs now, so it finally carries a baseline. Before that it could not be pinned at all:
a face on a periodic surface was split in one run and left whole in the next, and a regenerate run
refused to record anything. The volume never moved even then, which is why the geometry could be
judged while the partition still wandered.

WHAT WAS WRONG: the union did nothing at all. villarceauUnion came back as TWO solids of 147000 and
39463.13 - the slab and the torus, both unchanged and both complete - although the two bodies overlap
in half a torus, and no error was reported. Now it is ONE solid of 166739.027086 against the exact
147000 + 2000*pi^2 = 166739.2088021787, 1.1e-6.
The two halves were already right before the fix and still are:
  villarceauInter  19738.9967157   against the exact 2000*pi^2 = 19739.2088021787   1.1e-5
  villarceauRest   19739.016747    against the same exact half                      9.7e-6
  and against each other 1.0e-6, as the point reflection through the torus centre demands
Both have euler 1 - the pinch at the two tangential contacts - and so has the union.

Run this together with TorusVillarceauPlaneOblique: the two differ by a rotation of 37 degrees about
the z axis and nothing else, so their halves must measure the same, and they do to 5e-6. While the
union defect was open it hit only this one, the version whose contacts lie on the seam.
